name: Animemaxxing

lead:
Animemaxxing is a looksmax.org term for immersing oneself in anime. In one thread, a user listed his collection of figures, manga, keychains and other merchandise from a single series under the title.[1] The idea also covers styling hair and clothing after anime characters, which overlaps with cosplay and anime-inspired fashion.
The appearance angle is style: choosing haircuts, colours and outfits modelled on favourite characters. Cosplay, the established hobby behind this, uses costumes, wigs, makeup, hair dye and styling products to represent a character.[2]

paras: Practitioners range from collecting merchandise to wearing character-inspired outfits and hairstyles day to day. Cosplayers use commercial or self-made costumes, wigs, colored contacts and makeup.[2]

No physical risks beyond those of the individual products (dyes, colored contacts). Wearing costumes outside conventions is generally discouraged in Japan, though more common in the UK, US and Canada.[2]

Identity and community around the fandom
angle.text: Followers use anime character looks as a source for hair, colour and clothing choices, and the fandom as a social identity.

lead: Animemaxxing (anime maxxing) is a looksmax.org term for committing fully to anime fandom. In the thread that coined its use there, a member posted a photo and list of his collection of manga, figures, a nendoroid, keychains, a plush and artbooks from one series, and asked whether anyone else was 'AnimeMaxxing'.[1]

As a style meta it overlaps with cosplay, in which fans wear costumes and accessories to represent characters, often with wigs for unusual hair colours, makeup, coloured contact lenses, hair dye and styling products.[2] The term cosplay was coined in 1983 by Nobuyuki Takahashi of Studio Hard in My Anime magazine.[2]
No published studies have examined animemaxxing as an appearance strategy.

paras: The looksmax.org thread presenting the term was a collection post: a long list of merchandise from one series, with reaction pictures and a note that the user read the manga offline on his phone.[1]

Cosplayers use costumes from commercial makers, commissions or home sewing, and wigs, skin-tone makeup, colored contacts, temporary tattoos, hair dye and styling products to match characters.[2] Anime conventions are the main venues; Bilibili World in Shanghai reportedly had over 30,000 cosplayers in 2025.[3]

lore.intro: Discussed on looksmax.org as a fandom-and-collection identity.[1]

claims.claim: Anime fandom can be a lifestyle 'maxx' like any other

timeline.event: Nobuyuki Takahashi coins 'cosplay' in My Anime magazine.[2]
